record.original_question: Is every achievable Cantorval standard, in the sense that limsup |P_k|/r_k > 0 where |P_k| is the maximal length of E_k-intervals?

evidence.quote: A Cantorval E(xn) is called standard if limsup |Pk|/rk > 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(x_n)_{n\ge 1}$ be a non-increasing sequence of positive real numbers with $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} x_n < \infty$. The achievement set of $(x_n)$ is
$$E(x_n) = \Big\{ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n x_n : (\varepsilon_n) \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} \Big\}.$$
For each $k\ge 0$, let $r_k = \sum_{n>k} x_n$ and define
$$E_k = \Big\{ \sum_{n>k} \varepsilon_n x_n : (\varepsilon_n)_{n>k} \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} \Big\} \subseteq [0, r_k].$$
The set $E(x_n)$ is called a Cantorval if it is a non-empty compact set such that it is the closure of its interior, every point of $E(x_n)$ is an accumulation point, and both endpoints of every component interval of the complement of $E(x_n)$ are accumulation points of one-sided families of such component intervals from both sides. A Cantorval $E(x_n)$ is called achievable if it arises as the achievement set of some absolutely summable sequence as above.

Let $|P_k|$ denote the maximal length of a connected component (interval) appearing in $E_k$ (with $|P_k|=0$ if $E_k$ contains no nondegenerate interval). The Cantorval $E(x_n)$ is called standard if
$$\limsup_{k\to\infty} \frac{|P_k|}{r_k} > 0.$$

Question: Is every achievable Cantorval standard?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in the recent survey on achievement sets (2025/2026). Related recent work establishes standardness for specific classes (e.g., generalized Ferens Cantorvals) and studies Kakeya-type conditions, but no general resolution of the question for all achievable Cantorvals appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems including whether every achievable Cantorval is standard.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as an open problem in a current survey of achievement sets.

status_evidence.title: The Lebesgue measure of boundaries of multigeometric Cantorvals
status_evidence.snippet: All generalized Ferens Cantorvals satisfying (GF1) and (GF2) are standard Cantorvals.
status_evidence.claim: Standardness has been verified only for particular subclasses of achievable Cantorvals.

status_evidence.title: Achievable Cantorvals almost without reversed Kakeya conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Kakeya conditions and structure of achievable Cantorvals.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work focuses on related structural conditions but does not settle the standardness question in general.
